title: Put AI agents to work as players in Minecraft
summary: The yc-software team released a harness that lets AI models play Minecraft; they say they have run Bed Wars matches and a survival server with 50 agents.
agent_role: Each agent walks, mines, crafts, builds, fights and chats toward a goal the human types, keeps notes and writes small scripts in its own sandbox; the human sets the objective and can message it in game.
outcome: Authors report running Bed Wars matches and a survival server with 50 agents at once.
what_they_did: The team built a tool that connects an AI model to a Minecraft server as a regular player. You give it a goal like gathering wood and building a shelter. Each agent gets its own workspace for notes and small scripts. Teams of agents can message each other.
how_it_went: The authors say they have run Bed Wars matches with it and a survival server with 50 agents playing at once. No further results are given.
worth_knowing: Agents get a command shell by default; if no sandbox is set up, commands run on your own computer as you. Use the no-sandbox option to turn this off.
prompt: Set up the minecraft-agent-harness on my computer with the bundled test server and my [model provider] key. Start one agent named [agent name] with the goal: "[goal, e.g. gather wood and build a small shelter near spawn]". Run it without a command shell unless I approve one. Stream its actions, and after [number] minutes summarize what it did, where it got stuck, and what goal I should try next.

curation.rationale: A working harness with a concrete claim of Bed Wars matches and a 50-agent survival server, but outcomes are thin and the post is mostly setup and features.
